title: De Baptismo Primum
author: Concilia Carthaginiensia
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0356.stoa002.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

passages.original: Postquam in Africana Ecclesia Agrippino, vel etiam Tertulliano auctore, usus rebaptizandi cos qui ab haereticis baptizati erant, jam diu antehac frequentatus fuisset, eamque Novatianus, ut saltem hoc modo lapsos, quos immundos esse docebat, per Baptismum ab omni sua immunditia ablutos in Ecclesiam reciperet, aemulatus fuisset;
passages.english: After the practice of rebaptizing those who had been baptized by heretics had long been current in the African Church, on the authority of Agrippinus, or even of Tertullian, and Novatian had imitated it, so that in this way at least he might receive into the Church the lapsed, whom he taught were unclean, washed by Baptism from all their uncleanness;
passages.notes: 'cos' is a scanning error for 'eos' (those). 'eamque' (feminine) refers loosely back to the practice (usus, masculine), presumably understood as consuetudo; translated by sense.

passages.original: Ex episcopis primi reperiuntur fuisse Numidae, qui de iterando haereticorum Baptismate ad Cyprianum aliosque episcopos, ad synodum hanc Carthagine coactos, litteras conscripserunt. Prima igitur synodica hac de re consultatio, anno 258 48 Valeriani et Gallieni imperatorum 4, habita haec est, ut Cypriani Epistola 73, ad Jubaianum ostendit, in qua cum ex Africanis alii, juxta apostolicam traditionem sentirent non esse rebaptizandos eos qui legitime ab haereticis baptizati sunt : alii vero contra existimarent, unum Baptismum duntaxat esse unius Ecclesiae, ideoque apud haereticos qui extra Ecclesiam sunt, Baptismum 1036 verum et catho- licum esse non posse;
passages.english: Among the bishops, the first are found to have been the Numidians, who wrote a letter about repeating the Baptism of heretics to Cyprian and the other bishops gathered at Carthage for this synod. This, then, was the first synodal consultation on this matter, held in the year 258, the 4th [year] of the emperors Valerian and Gallienus, as Cyprian's Letter 73, to Jubaianus, shows. In it, while some of the Africans held, in accordance with apostolic tradition, that those who had been lawfully baptized by heretics were not to be rebaptized, others on the contrary thought that there is only one Baptism, belonging to the one Church, and that therefore among heretics, who are outside the Church, Baptism could not be true and catholic;
passages.notes: The figures '48' and '1036' appear to be stray marginal or page numbers from the printed edition and have been omitted. The date 258 is as printed; it does not sit easily with 'the 4th year of Valerian and Gallienus' (c. 256–257).
